KNP2.title: Two knights can't mate a bare king. Unless Black has a pawn #shorts
KNP2.desc:
With no pawn, 1.Kg6 would be stalemate. With the pawn, Black has to push it: 1.Kg6 a4 2.Nf6 a3 3.Nf7#. The extra pawn is the reason Black loses.

Did you know this one?

#chess #checkmate #chessendgame

KVNP.title: A whole knight against one pawn. Who wins? #shorts
KVNP.desc:
The knight stands right next to the corner, but after 1.h7 it needs f7 or g6 to guard h8, and from g8 it can reach neither (only e7, f6 and h6). So 2.h8=Q, and the pawn wins. Knights hate the edge of the board.

Did you guess right?

QRCE.title: Black just made a queen. Two moves later, she's gone #shorts
QRCE.desc:
Both pawns race. 1...h1=Q 2.a8=Q+ gives check along the long diagonal, the king has to step off it, and 3.Qxh1 takes the queen behind him. It's called a skewer.

Did you see it coming?

M2PZ.title: Mate in two. Can you find it? #shorts
M2PZ.desc:
White to move: 1.Qg8+! Rxg8 (forced, the knight guards g8) 2.Nf7#. The king is buried by his own rook and pawns. It's called a smothered mate.

Did you find it before the answer?

GST3.title: White is one move from checkmate. Then he plays this #shorts
GST3.desc:
Queen and king against king. Qg6 takes every square from the king, but it isn't check, so it's stalemate and a draw. Any check on the h-file (Qh4 or Qh1) was mate.

KV2P.title: The king stands between two loose pawns. Can he stop both? #shorts
KV2P.desc:
He can catch either one, he stands inside the square of both. But while he runs after one, the other runs too: 1...Kf4 2.a5 Kg4 3.a6 Kxh4 4.a7 and 5.a8=Q. One king can't stop two pawns this far apart.

Did you know the square rule?

#chess #chessendgame #pawnendgame

PNMT.title: This pawn is pinned, and it still protects the queen #shorts
PNMT.desc:
1.Qg7#. The queen's only guard is the f6 pawn, and the f8 rook pins it to the white king. But a pinned piece still gives check, so Kxg7 is illegal, and it's checkmate.

Did you know this rule?

#chess #chessrules #checkmate

WFM3.title: White's fastest checkmate takes three moves #shorts
WFM3.desc:
1.e4 g5 2.d4 f6 3.Qh5#. The king can't move, and nothing can block the check on the e8-h5 diagonal. Black's fastest mate, Fool's Mate, takes two.
